flags: minor: x > 0 condition correctly excludes x = -4 (which would give 20); fine as written
Q029-01.notes: x^2+x-12=(x+4)(x-3)=0, x>0 so x=3; x^2-x=9-3=6. Equivalent shortcut: x^2-x = 12-2x = 6. One factoring step plus substitution; graphing also works.

Q029-02.notes: g(x)=mx+4. g(3)=3m+4, g(1)=m+4; 3m+4=2m+8 gives m=4. Checked: m=0 -> 4 vs 8; m=8 -> 28 vs 24; m=16 -> 52 vs 40. Only B works.

flags: minor: easy elimination - C and D are clearly unsupported (equal means say nothing about median; D contradicts equal means), and A/B are direct opposites, so the item reduces to recalling what SD measures
Q029-03.notes: Larger SD (12 vs 5) means more spread. C not determined by mean/SD; D impossible with equal means.

flags: minor: closely mirrors a well-known released SAT item (3x - y = 12, 8^x/2^y); consider changing the structure so it is not recognizable
Q029-04.notes: 8^x/4^y = 2^(3x)/2^(2y) = 2^(3x-2y) = 2^7 = 128. Requires rewriting bases as powers of 2 - one key insight; students unfamiliar with it may stall, but it's a standard SAT pattern.

flags: minor: trap choice B (only x = 1) is the intended distractor; distractors A and D are weak
Q029-05.notes: f(1)=1-3+2=0. x^2-3x+2=0 -> (x-1)(x-2)=0, x=1 or 2: two values. Any non-vertex output of a quadratic is hit twice; x=1 is not the vertex (1.5).

Q029-06.notes: Multiply by 6: 2x + 3y = 6. B swaps coefficients (common error), A/D forget to scale the right side. Single routine step.
